NCT:
Column Name: NCT
Definition: "National Clinical Trial identifier, a unique identification number assigned to a clinical trial."

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for the term "NCT" followed by a unique identifier, usually a string of numbers.
- Step 2: Verify that the identified string matches the standard NCT format (e.g., NCTXXXXXXXX).
- Step 3: If multiple NCT numbers are present, extract all of them.
- Step 4: If no NCT number is found, mark "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the extracted string is a valid NCT identifier format.
- Do not extract any other identifier that is not an NCT number.
PubMed ID:
Column Name: PubMed ID
Definition: A unique identifier assigned to a clinical trial publication in the PubMed database.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Locate the PubMed ID, which is typically a numerical string, often labeled as "PMID" or "PubMed ID".
- Step 2: Verify that the identified string is a valid PubMed ID format (usually a series of digits).
- Step 3: Extract the numerical string.
- Step 4: If no PubMed ID is found, mark "not present".

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the extracted ID is a numerical string and not any other identifier.
- Do not confuse with other IDs like clinical trial registration numbers.
Trial Name:
Column Name: Trial Name
Definition: The title or identifier of the clinical trial being referred to in the study.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for a title or identifier that is explicitly described as the name of a clinical trial. This may be found in the title, abstract, or introduction of the document.
- Step 2: Look for keywords or phrases such as "clinical trial," "study name," "trial identifier," or "protocol number" that may precede or accompany the trial name.
- Step 3: Extract the full name or identifier of the trial, ensuring that it is not a reference to a different study or publication.
- Step 4: If no trial name or identifier is explicitly stated, mark as "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Be careful not to confuse the trial name with the publication title or other study identifiers.
- Ensure the extracted name is the full and correct name of the clinical trial.
Author:
Column Name: Author
Definition: The name of the person or people responsible for writing or publishing the clinical trial study.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Locate the author information, typically found at the beginning of the document, often in the header or title page.
- Step 2: Extract the full names of all listed authors.
- Step 3: If multiple authors are listed, record all names separated by commas or semicolons.
- Step 4: If no author information is explicitly stated, search for a section labeled "Authors," "Contributors," or similar.
- Step 5: If no author information can be found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure all author names are extracted completely and accurately.
- Do not include affiliations or other information, only the names of the authors.
- If the author is a group or organization, record the full name of the group or organization.
Year:
Column Name: Year
Definition: The year in which the clinical trial was published.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Locate the publication date of the clinical trial document. This is typically found near the title, in the header, or in the publication information section.
- Step 2: Identify the year from the publication date. The year should be a four-digit number (e.g., 2023, 2024).
- Step 3: If the publication date is not explicitly stated, look for a copyright date or a date of acceptance. Use the year from these dates if the publication date is unavailable.
- Step 4: If no date information is found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the extracted year is the publication year, not the year the study was conducted or the year the data was collected.
- If multiple dates are present, prioritize the publication date.
- If only a month and year are given, extract the year.
Full Pub or Abstract:
Column Name: Full Pub or Abstract
Definition: Indicates whether the study results were fully published or only an abstract is available.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search the document for explicit statements indicating whether the study is a "full publication," "full paper," "complete manuscript," or if it is an "abstract," "conference abstract," or "poster presentation."
- Step 2: If the document is an abstract, confirm that it is explicitly labeled as such (e.g., "Abstract" at the beginning of the document).
- Step 3: If the document is a full publication, look for indicators such as a journal name, volume, issue, and page numbers.
- Step 4: If the document is neither a full publication nor an abstract, or if it is unclear, mark the column as "not present."
- Step 5: If the document is a full publication, extract the text "Full Pub". If the document is an abstract, extract the text "Abstract".

Key Reminders:
- Do not assume a document is a full publication just because it is lengthy. Look for explicit indicators.
- Be careful not to confuse a full publication with a pre-print or a manuscript submitted for publication.
- If the document is a full publication, it should have a journal name, volume, issue, and page numbers.
Phase:
Column Name: Phase
Definition: "The stage or step in the clinical trial process, typically denoted by a Roman numeral (e.g. I, II, III, IV), which defines the scope, objectives, and duration of the trial."

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for the term "Phase" followed by a Roman numeral (I, II, III, or IV) or the full word (e.g., "Phase One," "Phase Two").
- Step 2: Verify that the identified Roman numeral or word is associated with the clinical trial being described in the document.
- Step 3: Extract the Roman numeral (e.g., "III") or the full word (e.g., "Phase Two") representing the trial phase.
- Step 4: If no phase is explicitly stated, search for terms like "early phase," "late phase," or "pivotal trial" which might imply the phase. If these are found, use them to infer the phase if possible (e.g., "pivotal trial" often implies Phase III).
- Step 5: If no phase information can be found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the Roman numeral is correctly interpreted (e.g., "II" is not confused with "III").
- If the phase is described in words (e.g., "Phase One"), extract the corresponding Roman numeral ("I").
- If multiple phases are mentioned, extract the phase that is most relevant to the primary study being described.
- If a phase is implied but not explicitly stated, use caution and only infer if the implication is very clear.
Original/Follow Up:
Column Name: Original/Follow Up
Definition: The designation of the clinical trial as either an original study or a follow-up study.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for explicit statements indicating whether the study is an "original study," "primary study," or a "follow-up study."
- Step 2: Look for phrases that might imply a follow-up study, such as "extension study," "long-term follow-up," or "continuation of [previous study name]."
- Step 3: If the document mentions a previous study that this study is based on, and the current study is examining long-term outcomes or additional data, classify it as a "follow-up study."
- Step 4: If the study is the first of its kind or does not reference a prior study, classify it as an "original study."
- Step 5: If no clear designation is found, mark as "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Be careful not to confuse a study that includes a follow-up period within its design with a study that is a follow-up to a previous study.
- If the study is an analysis of data from a previous study, it should still be classified as a follow-up study.
Number of Arms Included:
Column Name: Number of Arms Included
Definition: The total count of experimental treatment arms and control arms included in the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for explicit statements about the number of arms in the study, using phrases like "number of arms," "study arms," "treatment groups," or "experimental groups."
- Step 2: Identify and count each distinct treatment arm (e.g., "Arm A," "Arm B," "experimental arm 1," "experimental arm 2," "treatment group 1," "treatment group 2") and control arm (e.g., "control arm," "placebo arm," "standard of care arm").
- Step 3: Sum the number of treatment arms and control arms to get the total number of arms.
- Step 4: If the number of arms is stated directly (e.g., "This study included 3 arms"), extract that number.
- Step 5: If the number of arms is not explicitly stated, but each arm is described, count the number of arms based on the descriptions.
- Step 6: If no information about the number of arms or descriptions of arms is found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure that each arm is counted only once, even if it is mentioned multiple times.
- Be careful not to confuse subgroups within an arm with separate arms.
- If the study has a factorial design, count each unique combination of treatments as a separate arm.
- If the study has multiple phases, only count the arms included in the phase being analyzed.
Treatment Arm(s):
Treatment Arm(s)
Definition: Name of the experimental arm or arms in the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Identify sections of the document that describe the study design or methodology.
- Step 2: Look for explicit mentions of the experimental arm(s), treatment arm(s), or intervention group(s).
- Step 3: Extract the name(s) or description(s) of the treatment arm(s) exactly as they appear in the text.
- Step 4: If multiple treatment arms are present, extract all of them, separated by a comma.
- Step 5: If no treatment arm is explicitly named, mark as "not present".

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the extracted name is specific to the experimental arm and not the control arm.
- If the treatment arm is described by a drug name or intervention, extract that name.
- If the treatment arm is described by a code or abbreviation, extract that code or abbreviation.

Treatment Arm 1 Regimen

Total Participants - N:
Column Name: Total Participants - N
Definition: The total number of participants included in the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for phrases like "total participants," "number of patients," "sample size," or "participants enrolled."
- Step 2: Identify the numerical value associated with the total number of participants. This may be explicitly stated or found in the methods section.
- Step 3: If multiple numbers are present, ensure the number represents the total across all arms and not a subgroup.
- Step 4: If no such number is found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the number represents the total participants in the entire study, not just a specific arm or subgroup.
- Be careful not to confuse this with the number of participants in a specific analysis or subgroup.
Treatment Arm - N:
Column Name: Treatment Arm - N
Definition: The number of participants included in the experimental arm of the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Identify the section of the document that describes the study design and participant enrollment.
- Step 2: Look for explicit mentions of the "experimental arm," "treatment arm," "active treatment group," or similar terms.
- Step 3: Locate the number of participants assigned to this specific arm. This may be denoted as "n=", "N=", or "number of patients."
- Step 4: If multiple treatment arms exist, ensure the number corresponds to the correct experimental arm as defined in the study.
- Step 5: If the number of participants for the treatment arm cannot be found, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Be precise in identifying the correct treatment arm if multiple arms are present.
- Do not confuse the total number of participants with the number in the treatment arm.
- If the number is given as a range, extract the specific number if available, otherwise note the range.
Control Arm - N:
Column Name: Control Arm - N
Definition: The number of participants included in the control arm of the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Identify sections of the document that describe the study design or participant enrollment.
- Step 2: Look for explicit mentions of the "control arm," "placebo arm," "standard of care arm," or similar terms.
- Step 3: Extract the number of participants specifically assigned to the control arm. This may be indicated by "n=" or "number of participants in the control arm is".
- Step 4: If the number is given as a range, extract the lower and upper bounds. If a single number is given, extract that number.
- Step 5: If no such number is found, conclude "not present".

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the number extracted is specifically for the control arm and not the treatment arm or the total study population.
- Be careful not to confuse the number of participants with other numbers, such as the number of events or the number of sites.
- If multiple control arms exist, extract the number for each control arm separately if possible, otherwise, extract the total number of participants in all control arms.
Median Follow-Up Duration (mo):
Column Name: Median Follow-Up Duration (mo)
Definition: The median length of time, measured in months, that participants in the clinical trial were followed up or monitored after the start of the trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for the phrase "median follow-up" or "median follow up" or "median duration of follow-up". Also look for variations such as "median time to follow-up" or "median observation period".
- Step 2: Identify the numerical value associated with the median follow-up duration. Ensure the unit is in months (mo). If the unit is in years, convert to months by multiplying by 12.
- Step 3: If the median follow-up duration is reported for different arms or subgroups, extract the overall median follow-up duration if available. If only arm-specific values are present, extract all of them and note the arm.
- Step 4: If the median follow-up duration is not explicitly stated, but a range is given, or if only the mean follow-up is given, mark the column as "not present".
- Step 5: If the follow-up duration is given in a different unit (e.g., days, weeks), convert it to months and note the original unit.
- Step 6: If multiple median follow-up durations are reported (e.g., for different analyses), extract the primary analysis's median follow-up duration. If it is unclear which is primary, extract all and note the context.
- Step 7: If no mention of median follow-up duration is found, mark the column as "not present".

Key Reminders:
- Ensure the extracted value is the *median* follow-up, not the mean or average.
- Pay close attention to the units (months). Convert if necessary.
- If multiple values are present, prioritize the overall median follow-up duration.
- If no median follow-up is explicitly stated, do not attempt to calculate it from other data.

Quality of Life reported:
Column Name: Quality of Life reported
Definition: Indicates whether the clinical trial reported results on the quality of life of participants.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for keywords or phrases related to "quality of life," such as "QoL," "patient-reported outcomes," "functional status," "well-being," or "health-related quality of life (HRQoL)."
- Step 2: If any of these terms are found within the context of the clinical trial's results or outcomes, extract the information and mark as "yes" or "reported".
- Step 3: If no such terms or related discussions are found, mark the column as "no" or "not reported".
- Step 4: If the document mentions quality of life but does not provide any results, mark as "mentioned but no results".

Key Reminders:
- Be sure to distinguish between a study that mentions quality of life as a goal and one that actually reports results.
- Look for explicit statements about the reporting of quality of life data, not just mentions of the concept.
- If there is ambiguity, err on the side of "not reported" unless there is clear evidence of results being presented.
Quality of Life Scale:
Column Name: Quality of Life Scale
Definition: A measure of the participants' overall well-being and satisfaction with their health status, as assessed through a standardized questionnaire or survey, reflecting their perceived quality of life during the clinical trial.

Detailed Extraction Instructions:
- Step 1: Search for mentions of "quality of life," "QoL," "well-being," "health status," or similar terms related to patient-reported outcomes.
- Step 2: Identify if a standardized questionnaire or survey was used to assess quality of life (e.g., "EORTC QLQ-C30," "FACT-P," "SF-36," or other named scales).
- Step 3: Extract the specific scale used and any reported scores, changes from baseline, or statistical comparisons between study arms.
- Step 4: Note if the data is presented as mean scores, medians, or other statistical measures, and extract the corresponding values.
- Step 5: If the quality of life data is presented graphically, attempt to extract the numerical values from the text or figure captions.
- Step 6: If no specific quality of life scale or data is mentioned, conclude "not present."

Key Reminders:
- Be specific about the scale used (e.g., "EORTC QLQ-C30" rather than just "QoL").
- Distinguish between different time points if multiple assessments are reported.
- If only partial data is available (e.g., only a change from baseline), note the partial availability.
- Do not infer quality of life scores if they are not explicitly stated.
